content:
Maria: Quick sync — thinking about autoscaler tradeoffs for dedicated GPU pools. TL;DR: prefer soft reservations + predictive headroom over hard pre-alloc. Thoughts?
Sam: Agree on soft reservations. Key Q: how does billing/accounting work if we prewarm? We need per-tenant warm credits.
Devon: +1 soft. Also need a circuit breaker for sudden cost spikes; recommend a leaky-bucket on tenant spend and a fast-path evict.
Maria: Proposed policy prototype (short):
```json
{
  "policy": "soft_reserve",
  "headroom_pct": 0.12,
  "prewarm_window_sec": 90,
  "burst_mode": "ephemeral",
  "cost_limit_per_hour_usd": 150
}
```
Sam: Small nit: 90s may be too short for some quantized fp16 models with cold KV loads. Suggest collecting startup_time per model and make window adaptive.
orch-bot: autoscaler:policy v2 applied to pool-dedicated-eu-west by Kevin.
Kevin: Can the admission surface handle mixed-model pools? e.g., 8-bit quant vs fp16 with different startup times and memory footprints.
Devon: We should tag models with metadata: startup_time_ms, prewarm_memory_mb, fallback_variant. Orch can use those tags for admission and prewarm sizing.
Maria: Also tradeoff: longer prewarm increases cost but reduces P99 + cold-start errors. Need SLA-aware default profiles per tenant tier (free/dev/prod).
Sam: Agree. Suggest A/B: run experiment with 60s vs 180s prewarm windows for a slice of production traffic and measure P99 latency, error-rate, and cost delta.
Kevin: Also need operator tooling — a console slider or policy override to adjust headroom across pools in real-time (with audit).
Devon: Edge-case: simultaneous multi-tenant bursts. Prioritize high-SLA tenants, spill best-effort to hosted fallback or queued admission. If fallback invoked, ensure tokens/trace include fallback_hint.
Maria: Fallback compatibility list is critical. Admission policy must know which hosted or lower-cost variants preserve quality.
Sam: Action items: (1) add startup_time + fallback_variant to model catalog; (2) prototype A/B prewarm windows; (3) add tenant-level cost caps and circuit-breaker hooks; (4) wire console override control.
Kevin: I'll own (1) and (3) — update model onboarding pipeline and admission quota service.
Devon: I'll run the A/B experiment and surface metrics. Need a per-tenant warm_hit_ratio metric (currently we only have per-pool).
Maria: I'll mock the console UI and draft the RFC follow-up with cost SLO tradeoffs.
Sam: One more ask: can we emit an event when autoscaler declines a request due to headroom? Need this for observability and customer-facing explanations.
Devon: We can add an `admission.decision` event with tags: tenant, model_tag, reason=(prewarm_limit|cost_cap|capacity).
Maria: Good — tie that into rollout telemetry and alerts. Also include a heatmap in the console for warm vs cold start by tenant.
Sam: :thumbsup:
Kevin: lgtm. When do we want the RFC?
Maria: Draft this week, send for review Monday.
orch-bot: INCIDENT RECORD: pool-dedicated-eu-west saw a +5% cost bump during last week's scale test. Logged to #incidents/1234.
Maria: Noted — will include the test results and cost delta in the RFC.
Sam: Thanks all — sync ended.
